statements.status_notes: Debian's tracker lists nmap 7.95+dfsg-3 on trixie as vulnerable with no fixed version (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2018-15173) and rates the issue unimportant with no security impact. Debian's rating is not relied on as evidence that the code is unreachable. The vulnerable code is present in this build, and the affected -sV (service version detection) path is reachable. No fixed release is available for this release line, so the assessment is under investigation.
This package backports the zero-length TCP option handling from upstream commit https://github.com/nmap/nmap/commit/7ef4ee030a0023fe22616387a000032e1a678b6a.
This package backports the bounds checks from upstream commit https://github.com/nmap/nmap/commit/bb6754e76bb1686315008e1aa1c40202a513fb83 before parsing IPv6 extension headers.

Debian's tracker lists nmap 7.95+dfsg-3 on trixie as vulnerable with no fixed version (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2018-15173) and rates the issue unimportant with no security impact. Debian's rating is not relied on as evidence that the code is unreachable. The vulnerable code is present in this build, and the affected -sV (service version detection) path is reachable. No fixed release is available for this release line, so the assessment is under investigation.
This package backports the zero-length TCP option handling from upstream commit https://github.com/nmap/nmap/commit/7ef4ee030a0023fe22616387a000032e1a678b6a.
This package backports the bounds checks from upstream commit https://github.com/nmap/nmap/commit/bb6754e76bb1686315008e1aa1c40202a513fb83 before parsing IPv6 extension headers.

The compatibility images ship Nmap and its NSE scripts. A zero-length TCP option can cause unbounded allocation in nselib/packet.lua. The upstream fix is commit 7ef4ee030a0023fe22616387a000032e1a678b6a, included in Nmap 7.991; a compatible packaged fix and its validation remain under investigation. See https://github.com/nmap/nmap/commit/7ef4ee030a0023fe22616387a000032e1a678b6a and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-72712

The compatibility images ship Nmap 7.95. Crafted truncated IPv6 extension headers can cause out-of-bounds reads and a scanner crash during raw IPv6 scans. The upstream fix is commit bb6754e76bb1686315008e1aa1c40202a513fb83; a compatible packaged fix and its validation remain under investigation. See https://github.com/nmap/nmap/commit/bb6754e76bb1686315008e1aa1c40202a513fb83 and https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-58058

The compatibility images ship the Nmap scanner, including service-version detection. A crafted TCP service response can exhaust the scanner stack during -sV scans. Debian tracks this as an unfixed issue with unimportant urgency; applicability and remediation remain under investigation. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2018-15173
